label: Builder.io
summary: Reads, drafts and (if you allow it) publishes content in the Builder.io spaces you connect on the Builder.io page and give to the worker, each with its own access.

coreWhy.files.read: Reads files the task refers to, such as page data to upload.
coreWhy.browser: Opens the site to check pages, when you allow it.

steps: Check which Builder spaces you have with builder_access_status; when there is more than one, name the space in every Builder call
Find what already exists (models, entries, the page's url) before creating anything
Update an existing entry rather than creating a second one for the same page
limits: Never create a second entry for content that already exists: update it.
Never claim a page is live unless builder_verify_content says servedAsLive: true.
Never write to a space builder_access_status says you may only read.
starters: List the models and pages in the Builder space, and say which are live. Don't change anything.

questions.label: Builder spaces it can use
questions.help: Spaces you connect on the Builder.io page. Give it each space it needs, read only or read and write. Production spaces are read-only: writes go only to spaces marked as test spaces, whatever you choose under content.

questions.label: Models and pages it works on
What may it do with content?
questions.help: Applies to the spaces it may write to (above). A production space is never written to, whatever you choose here.

choices.label: Prepare drafts; a person publishes
choices.approval: It saves drafts; publishing is yours (it has no publish tool).

choices.label: Create, update and publish
limits: Publish only when the task asks for it.
choices.approval: It can publish, in test spaces only.

relations.why: Reads the Figma designs the pages are built from.
Opens the site to check the published pages.

changes.1.1.0: Builder spaces are connected on the platform (Integrations → Builder.io), several per person, encrypted at rest. Each worker is given the spaces it may use, read only or read and write (new setting "Builder spaces it can use"; replaces the free-text "Builder space"). Writes go only to spaces given with write access that are marked as test spaces. The space mapping is never exported in a worker package: whoever installs it maps their own spaces.
